steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Old Dalton's death and Shelly freezing in the cold storage were no accidents...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Now Michael and Marion are dead too, in such a horrible way...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Who's behind all this? Why all the murders in the first place? And why are they so... gruesome?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I have a feeling that Michael saw this coming.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: He looked a lot more serious than usual when we met the night before the murder.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: He must've figured out the real reason Dalton died, panicked, and decided to get out of here, but...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Now we'll never know what he was hiding.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Maybe this all has to do with that accident five years ago, but what's really worrying me is that...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: The killer's not even trying to make them look like accidents anymore. What if they're trying to tell us—

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: That until the entire truth is brought to light, nobody is safe.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Omigosh, sorry Molly, did my babbling scare you?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Don't worry, it doesn't matter if there really is, like, a crazy killer running out there, I'll protect you no matter how many of them there are.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Oh, that's not it, Detective Tippi. I was just thinking about... what I can do on my end.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Michael's dead now, but that doesn't mean what he wanted me to do doesn't matter anymore.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: The killer might be planning on using the escape landboats Miss Stone mentioned for their next move...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: So if we can figure another way out, or put together something that'll get us to the ground, or even just find an exhaust vent...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: We might be able to get away from this maniac hiding in the shadows and save ourselves during the climax.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Molly...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Tippi, you were the first person to really open up to me after I joined the crew.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Even though I kept messing up and getting you into trouble, you were always there to stand up for me. When Marion would forget my name, you were always ready to give her a proper reminder.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: You're always looking after me, comforting me, protecting me...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: So this time, I want to protect you too.
The Liberi gives a gentle hug to her most precious friend in the whole crew.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Once this is all over, we're totally gonna have a movie marathon at your place. Twenty-four hours of non-stop screams, paired with our favorite drinks and fried finballs.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I wanna see what the house you grew up in looks like, and meet that sister you're always bragging about.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: ...Sure.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I'm terribly sorry to interrupt your little sorority huddle.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Oh, wow, Miss Rutherford? What brings you to the prop room? Where's your assistant?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Didn't you receive Greta's notice on your terminals? She's already sent out compensation to everyone and officially disbanded the crew.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Whether you're scared of the killer, worried about the Catastrophe, or want to stay and finish the shoot, we're all free to do as we please.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: So naturally it only took a blink of an eye for that spineless assistant of mine to run off god-knows-where.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Do as we please?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Don't tell me Miss Stone—no, none of the crew even care about the real reason all these murders are happening?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn, and I don't see why you should either. Surely the reasonable thing to do is escape and leave that to the police?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Or, as Greta said, you can leave the truth to whoever feels like playing detective.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: So, why'd you come looking for us, ma'am?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I'm only here for you, Tippi, the background painter.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I admire Greta's gumption in wanting to film a Catastrophe, and this is a fine opportunity for me as well, but films cannot rely solely on natural phenomena.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I know you're more passionate about cinema than most, and you must have heard how important this project is to me.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: So I implore you, from the bottom of my heart, to put your talent in ambience-building and color-matching to work, and paint the perfect backdrop for my grand finale.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Wow...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I mean, I'd totally love to, but...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Go help her out, Tippi.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Hey, Molly, what's with the raincoat? Are you really going 'exploring'?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Don't worry, I've been part of the prop team for ages now, and I know my way around the plate. I'll be fine.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Remember what we were just talking about? This is something I need to do.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Alright then.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Once I'm done helping out with the backdrops, I'll come find you, promise!

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You may enter, Madam Stone.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: You know it was me before I even opened the door?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Yes. I have been waiting for you.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Your little investigation the other day forced me to reveal my plan of filming a real Catastrophe to the whole crew.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: The timing couldn't have been worse. Abner and the rest of the crew were already unhappy with me. So I had to make some last-minute decisions. Big decisions.

spans.text: The timing couldn't have been worse. Abner and the rest of the crew were already unhappy with me. So I had to make some last-minute decisions.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: If I wanted to, I could sue you for damages incurred by your act of industrial sabotage, Lucian.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: But?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: But I'm not going to punish my cast just to vent or assert my authority, especially when such actions would only complicate the situation.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: And then, more murders. The killer even stopped hiding their savagery, and everyone's losing their minds, except you. You're the same as ever, cool as a cucumber, watching the crowd from a distance.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I suppose I can thank this crisis for making it clear that you have other reasons to be here.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: But none of that's important right now. The crew's been disbanded. You can leave, or stay until the date specified in the contract. It's up to you.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Your part in this is done anyway.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Hardly.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: The moment you came to find me, you proved that my part in this is not yet done.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: ...I can't magic up another Lady Dupont, or bring the three Rockefeller brothers back to life.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: We're running out of both time and manpower. So I need to figure out the best use of our limited resources.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Lucian, I'd like you to be the lead for the rest of the film.
In the middle of the night, the clackety-clack of typing echoes through the office.
A despondent Perro curls up in front of his typewriter. He glances at his latest manuscript, and stubs a cigarette out on it.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Ending, ending, ending...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Lady Dupont needs to die in the ending...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: 'After she elopes with the second Rockefeller, they vanish from high society and live a poetic life out in the countryside.'

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: 'But Rockefeller's life of affluence has left too much of a mark on him. He eventually shames Lady Dupont for her empty family name and leaves her. In despair, she slits her own throat...'

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Too realistic...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: And do they really have to be punished after leaving their extravagant lives behind?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: This takes place back when Columbia held wealth as its highest virtue. I'm just trying to recreate it and let the audience judge for themselves!
The little cigarette burn grows, spreads, and swallows the whole paper up. Steven takes a deep breath and blows away the ashes.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: 'In the end, Lady Dupont chooses none of the Rockefellers. She had only wanted to escape her false destiny through marriage, but underestimated just how toxic love can be.'

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: 'The brothers, unbeknownst to each other, each plot their own revenge, and Lady Dupont is killed by three different schemes at the same time.'

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: No, too lowbrow...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Getting stuck in a quagmire of love even after not choosing anyone makes it sound like it's fate at work, but it's really just slapping in a trope to patch up the gaps.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: The final shot of her body being pulverized into nothing would definitely be shocking, but the setup's just too crude.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: 'The Dupont's family's false claims of being descended from Victorian nobility are finally exposed to the public. No matter how deep the Rockefeller brothers' love for her is, they cannot shield her from punishment.'

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: 'The only time in her life that Lady Dupont is treated as true nobility is when the real Dupont family demands the death penalty for her...'

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: It's too... neat!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: All tied up with a bow to show off how deep and meaningful it is, but it lacks any of the madness or romance a film called The Death of Lady Dupont should have!

spans.text: All tied up with a bow to show off how deep and meaningful it is, but it lacks any of the madness or romance a film called

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Tch, out of draft paper. Let me fetch some more from the filing cabinet...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Whoa!
Steven slips on a wad of paper he threw to the ground earlier, falling flat on his back.
Only now does he notice that the entire office is filled with discarded drafts. There is nowhere left for him to stand.
He lies down amidst his aborted ideas, covering his face with his hands as he yells in frustration.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Get a Kubricking grip, Steven Quay! You've been messing with the ending for two whole months now, and don't even have a shitty half-baked scene to show for it!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: This is your baby! You wrote every damn line in this story! Don't tell me you don't even know what you want to write?!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: If you need to suffer to make a classic, then this must be a goddamn masterpiece, right?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: You've got the time pressure of the shooting, the shock of hearing about filming a Catastrophe, the fear of some maniac going around killing the crew... You got it all, man! What more could you want?!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: 'God of Inspiration', my ass!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: That was just some stupid excuse to get Greta off your back. Your god ain't coming—you lost his Falking contact details!

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Who's there...?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: ...Well, honestly, I don't care who you are, as long as you can help me figure out this ending.
